rule.description: One geographic location, whose latitude and longitude belong together in use, meaning and lifetime, is repeatedly handled as two separate scalar values instead of one grouped location value, either as two parameters of a callable or as two sibling class/interface members.

checks.description: Detect every call site owner and every data owner that splits the location into a bare latitude value and a bare longitude value, with one grouped location value nowhere in the signature or member list.
checks.detected_relation: location -> {latitude parameter/member, longitude parameter/member} split across one signature or one owning class
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The latitude and longitude of one location are always used together to mean the same geographic point, yet each callable or owner repeats them as unrelated scalar values, forcing every producer and consumer to split and re-pair the same pair at each boundary.

matches.evidence: Validate the scalar coordinate parts: validateLocationParts(latitude, longitude) receives location[0] and location[1] separately from validateLocation and re-pairs them into an array only to format its error message.

Encode the hash from scalars in algorithm order: geohashEncodeBits(longitude, latitude, precision) receives the pair in reversed slot order from geohashForLocation, which destructures location before the call.
boundingBoxPoints(latitude, longitude, radius) receives the pair as two of three parameters from boundingBoxCoordinates, with the independent radius sitting directly after the pair.

haversineKilometers(latitude1, longitude1, latitude2, longitude2) carries two locations as four scalar parameters, numbered to keep the two pairs apart; callers must interleave destruction of two tuples to invoke it.

encodeGeoFireObject(latitude, longitude, geohash) splits the stored location into two scalar parameters next to the derived geohash, and re-pairs them as a fresh array for validation and for the stored 'l' field.

GeoQuery stores the query center as two sibling scalar fields _centerLat and _centerLng instead of one location value, so every consumer (_listenForNewGeohashes, updateCriteria, center(), _distanceToCenter) re-pairs the center into an array before use.

GeoQuery._updateLocation(key, latitude, longitude) receives the incoming location already split; it validates, hashes, stores and fires callbacks with re-paired [latitude, longitude] arrays at four separate places in the body.

GeoQuery._distanceToCenter(latitude, longitude) re-pairs its two parameters and the two center fields into arrays just to call the public distanceBetween, threading four scalar pieces through one helper.

excluded.reason: Adjacent numeric parameters (distance, latitude) where the distance is genuinely independent of the coordinate slot; a herring that the rule correctly leaves out.
Adjacent numeric parameters (resolution, latitude); the resolution is not part of a location pair.
Two geohash-related parameters; geohash is derived data, not a second coordinate slot.
Passes an already-grouped location value; this is the public callback contract that must remain unchanged, not a manifestation of the clump.
A different cohesive group (query configuration object); its center is already stored grouped, so it is outside the split-pair relation.
The tracked-location record keeps 'location' as one grouped value; splitting its remaining members is a different data group outside this rule.
